name: Competing dominant primary controls
summary: Several identically emphasized 'main' actions within the same immediate choice set may compete for attention and make next-step selection less clear.
recurring_structure: Multiple equally prominent primary/default-emphasis controls placed in one connected decision group without a clear task distinction.
harm_mechanism: Competing strongest emphasis can obscure the intended principal action; GOV.UK identifies next-step confusion while Primer restricts primary emphasis in groups.
context: Single-page/single-group decisions that have one main progression and optional subsidiary alternatives.
applicability: Same group with competing primary treatments not explained by distinct user goals.
legitimate_contexts: Independent task zones on the same page with separate local priorities.
Balanced equally significant alternatives; not every multi-button group is a failure.

usability: Potentially harder identification of the next step as described by GOV.UK; not independently measured in this run.
accessibility: Visual emphasis is not equivalent to keyboard/focus/name-role accessibility; no WCAG failure inferred.

counterexamples.summary: Separate unrelated action groups can legitimately each highlight their own main operation.
counterexamples.context: Page composed of independent tasks; confirmation requires user-context research.

version_context: GOV.UK and Primer live unversioned documentation retrieved 2026-10-08
